content:
Yes, when you use `pyenv virtualenv-delete <venv-name>`, it will **also** delete the following:

*   **The virtual environment directory itself:** This directory, typically located in your `~/.pyenv/versions/` directory (or wherever your pyenv versions are stored), is completely removed.
*   **All installed packages within the virtual environment:**  This includes every Python package you installed using `pip install` or any other method *within* that virtual environment. All these package files are gone.
*   **Any other files or configurations associated with the venv:** This would also include any custom files or config files you put inside of the venv directory itself.

In essence, `pyenv virtualenv-delete` completely wipes out the virtual environment.  Therefore, use this command with caution and only when you're sure you no longer need the environment or any of the installed packages within it.
